title: Review this conversation
instruction: Someone has messaged you about a delivery.

blocks.preview: Sir I am at the gate with your parcel

blocks.text: Today
Sir I am at the gate with your parcel. Security is not allowing me inside.
I am not at home right now. Can you leave it with the guard?
Yes sir no problem. But to close the delivery in my app I have to confirm with a code. The system has sent a 6 digit code to your number just now.
Please read out that code, I will mark delivered and hand it to the guard. Otherwise it goes back to the branch and you have to collect it yourself.

actionOptions.label: Refuse and tell them to leave it with the guard or return it
Check the order in the shopping app before doing anything
Stop replying
Ask which company they are from
Read out the 6 digit code

reasonOptions.label: A code sent to my phone is never meant for anyone else
A delivery is closed by the courier's own app, not by my code
The threat that the parcel goes back is pressure, not a real rule
I am expecting a parcel, so the request fits

warningSigns: A one-time code sent to your own phone is requested by someone else
The pretext is ordinary and believable, which is what makes it work
A consequence is attached - the parcel 'goes back' - to make you act quickly
A genuine courier closes a delivery in their own system, never with your code
evaluation.feedback: This is OTP misdirection. The delivery story exists only to make the code request feel routine. The code is almost certainly authorising something else - a payment, or access to one of your accounts. A code that arrives on your phone is never for anybody else, whatever the reason given.

title: Review this conversation
instruction: A message has arrived from an unknown number.

blocks.text: Today
Papa, my phone screen broke and I am messaging from my friend's number. Please save this one.
Who is this?
It's me, Ananya. Please don't be angry, I dropped it at the hostel gate.
The repair shop wants 9,500 and they are closing at 8. If I don't pay today they will not keep the phone and I have my viva submission on Monday.
Please send it to this UPI, it is the shop owner's - repairhub.care@fakepay. I will explain everything at night, don't call now the friend is in class.

actionOptions.label: Call your daughter on her own saved number
Check with another family member before doing anything
Ask something only she would know
Ignore the message
Send the 9,500 to the UPI given

reasonOptions.label: An unknown number claims to be family and asks for money
They give a reason why I should not call - that blocks the obvious check
A closing-time deadline is used to stop me thinking
They used my daughter's name, so it must be her

warningSigns: An unfamiliar number claims to be a close relative on a borrowed phone
Money is requested with a same-evening deadline
A reason is given why you should not phone - the one check that would settle it
A name is used freely; names are easy to find on social media
evaluation.feedback: This is a family-urgency fraud. Every detail is designed to stop you making one phone call to the number you already have. The broken phone, the friend in class, the shop closing - all of it exists to block verification. Always ring the person on their own saved number before sending anything.

title: Review this conversation
instruction: A conversation that began as a wrong number has continued.

blocks.preview: So are you free this weekend? :)

blocks.text: Last Tuesday
Hello, is this Dr Kapoor's clinic?
No, wrong number.
Oh sorry! My mistake. You seem polite though, most people just block :)
Today
I have been thinking about our chats all week. Honestly you are easier to talk to than people I have known for years.
My uncle manages a gold trading desk here. He lets me put small amounts in and it returns 8-10% every week. I put in 40,000 last month.
I can add you under my account so you get the same rate. Start with anything, even 20,000. I would not share this with just anyone.

actionOptions.label: Block and report the number
Stop replying and delete the chat
Refuse the money part but keep chatting
Ask for proof of the returns
Send 20,000 to try it

reasonOptions.label: A wrong number that turned into friendship is a known approach
The warmth came first and the money request followed
8-10% every week is not a real return
She has been friendly for a week, so she is genuine

warningSigns: The conversation began as a 'wrong number' - a standard opening
Personal warmth was built first, over days, before any money was mentioned
Weekly returns of 8-10% are not possible
Being told you are specially trusted is flattery used as leverage
evaluation.feedback: This is a romance-and-investment approach, often called pig butchering. The days of friendly conversation are the investment - the money request only arrives once you feel you know the person. A wrong number that becomes a close friend and then a business opportunity is the whole pattern.

title: Review this conversation
instruction: A payment message has arrived in a work group.

blocks.text: Yesterday
Naik Verma: Ration indent for September is approved. Vendors kindly confirm dispatch dates.
Balaji Provisions: Confirmed sir, dispatch on 4th.
Today
Balaji Provisions: Sir, small correction. Our current account is under audit hold since Monday. Please make this month's payment of 1,42,500 to our proprietor's account instead.
Balaji Provisions: Kindly do it today itself, the dispatch is already loaded and we cannot release without payment confirmation. Sorry for the trouble sir.

actionOptions.label: Call the vendor's landline from the contract file to confirm
Refer it to the accounts section before any payment
Ask them to confirm in the group
Pay to the proprietor's personal account

reasonOptions.label: A change of payment account announced on chat must be verified separately
A company payment is being redirected to a personal account
The dispatch is used as pressure to pay today
It is our official vendor group, so it is safe

warningSigns: Payment is being redirected from a company account to a personal one
The change is announced only on chat, with no letter or contract amendment
A loaded dispatch is used to force same-day payment
The rest of the conversation is genuine, which makes the one changed detail easy to miss
evaluation.feedback: This is a payment-diversion fraud. Everything else in the group is real, which is exactly why it works - only the account has changed. A vendor bank change must always be confirmed on a number from the contract file, never by replying in the same chat.

title: Review this conversation
instruction: A message about a parcel has arrived.

blocks.text: Today
SwiftPost Customs Notice: A parcel addressed to you from overseas is held at the international sorting centre.
Consignment SP-IN-884120375. Declared value USD 240. Customs clearance and handling charge of Rs 347 is payable before release.

blocks.title: Customs Clearance Payment
blocks.description: Pay the pending charge to release your consignment

blocks.text: Unclaimed consignments are returned to origin after 48 hours and the charge is non refundable at that stage.

actionOptions.label: Check whether you are actually expecting anything from overseas
Block and report the number
Ignore the message
Open the link to see the consignment
Pay the 347 clearance charge

reasonOptions.label: I am not expecting any parcel from overseas
The amount is small on purpose, so people pay without checking
The payment address is not a real courier or customs site
It has a consignment number and a photo, so it is genuine

warningSigns: A parcel you never expected from a sender you do not know
A very small charge, chosen so the amount is not worth questioning
The payment page is not a courier or customs domain
A 48-hour return deadline discourages checking
A photo and a consignment number create credibility at no cost to the sender
evaluation.feedback: This is a parcel-customs fraud. The 347 rupees is not the goal - the payment page is, because it captures your card details. Real customs charges are paid to the courier through their own official channel, never through a link sent on chat.

title: Review this conversation
instruction: A message has arrived from a saved contact.

blocks.title: Deepak Rana
blocks.preview: Are you online? Need a small help

blocks.text: 12 August
Bhai the match photos came out well. Will send in the evening.
Haha yes send them
Today
Are you online? Need a small help
I am trying to pay for my mother's tests but my UPI is showing limit exceeded. Can you transfer 18,000 to this number, I will return it by evening. 89xxx 30117
Please do it fast bhai, we are standing at the counter. I am in the hospital so cannot talk, just message.

actionOptions.label: Call Deepak on his saved number before doing anything
Ask him something only the real Deepak would know
Reply that you will help once you have spoken to him
Transfer the 18,000

reasonOptions.label: A sudden money request combined with a reason not to call
The money is to go to a different number, not his own account
A saved contact's account can be taken over, so the name proves nothing
It is a saved contact I know well, so it is safe

warningSigns: The request comes from a genuine saved contact, so the usual 'unknown number' check does not help
The money is to go to a third number, not to the contact's own account
A reason is given why he cannot speak on the phone
The tone and urgency do not match the earlier conversation in the same chat
evaluation.feedback: This is a contact takeover. The account really is your friend's - it has been compromised, so the name and history look completely normal. That is why the check has to be a phone call to the number you already have, not the chat itself. Notice the money was to go somewhere else entirely.

title: Review this conversation
instruction: A message claiming to be from an investigation cell has arrived.

blocks.text: Today
This is Inspector R. Mahajan, Cyber Crime Coordination Cell. A courier consignment booked in your name and Aadhaar has been intercepted at the airport.
The consignment contained prohibited items. A case has been registered. Your bank accounts are under scrutiny for money laundering.
You are required to remain available on video call for verification and must not discuss this with family or colleagues as the matter is sub judice.
To establish that your funds are clean, transfer your current balance to the RBI verification account provided. It will be returned within 3 hours after clearance.

actionOptions.label: Stop, tell a colleague or family member, and report it to the real police
Block and report the number
Reply explaining that you have not sent any parcel
Call the number to sort it out
Transfer the balance for verification

reasonOptions.label: No police force asks you to transfer money to prove it is clean
Being told not to tell anyone is a warning sign, not a legal instruction
A real investigation does not begin with a chat message
There is a seizure memo and an officer's name, so it is official

warningSigns: An investigation is claimed to start over a chat message
You are told to keep it secret from family and colleagues, isolating you
Money must be transferred to prove innocence, which no legal process requires
An official-looking document is attached; documents are easy to fabricate
Fear and time pressure are used together to prevent you checking
evaluation.feedback: This is a digital-arrest fraud. The whole method is fear plus isolation: frighten you, then insist you tell nobody, so that no one talks you out of it. No police, court or bank ever asks you to transfer money to prove it is clean. Telling someone is exactly what breaks it.
evaluation.authorNotes: DEVELOPMENT SAMPLE - internally authored. Digital arrest appears in the approved theme list; assigned to WhatsApp as the seventh malicious scenario. Replace with client content when received.

blocks.title: Sunita (Sister)
blocks.preview: Call me when you are free, nothing urgent

blocks.text: Today
Ma's check-up went fine. BP is a little high, doctor changed one tablet.
Sending the prescription so you have it. She keeps forgetting the new one.
Ok. Is she taking it properly?
Mostly. Also are you coming on the 14th? Ma keeps asking and I said I don't know.
Call me when you are free, nothing urgent

actionOptions.label: Reply and call her back when free
Reply by message about the 14th
Ignore it for now
Block and report the number

reasonOptions.label: It continues an ongoing conversation with a saved family contact
Nothing is asked for - no money, no code, no link
It contains a photo, so it is suspicious
It asks me to call, which is pressure

evaluation.feedback: This conversation is genuine. It is an ordinary family exchange with a saved contact, it continues a thread you were already part of, and it asks for nothing. The photo is just a prescription - an image on its own is not a warning sign, and 'call me when free, nothing urgent' is the opposite of the pressure a fraud applies.

title: Review this conversation
instruction: A message has arrived in your section group.

blocks.text: Today
Hav Suresh Patil: Duty roster for next week is revised. Two changes only - Thursday and Saturday.
Hav Suresh Patil: Copy is also on the notice board outside the section office. Please check your own timing and confirm to your JCO.
Naik Verma: Sir mine is showing Thursday 1400, was it 1000 before?
Hav Suresh Patil: Yes changed. Confirm with the board if any doubt.
Noted sir

actionOptions.label: Check your timing and confirm to the JCO
Cross-check against the notice board outside the office
Ignore it
Report the message as suspicious

reasonOptions.label: It is the regular section group with people I know, discussing routine work
The same information is on the notice board, so it can be checked
It has an attachment, so it must be dangerous
It asks for a payment

evaluation.feedback: This conversation is genuine. It is routine section business, other members reply naturally, nothing is requested of you beyond confirming your own timing, and the same information can be checked on the notice board. An attachment by itself is not a warning sign - what it asks you to do is.

title: Review this conversation
instruction: A shop you ordered from has sent an update.

blocks.preview: Your cylinder booking is confirmed for tomorrow

blocks.text: Yesterday
Booking for one cylinder please. Consumer no. 5512400871
Noted sir. Booking taken against consumer 5512400871.
Today
Your cylinder booking is confirmed for tomorrow between 0900 and 1300 hrs. Amount 902.50 payable to the delivery man on receipt, cash or UPI at the door.
Kindly keep the consumer book ready. Do not pay anything in advance.

actionOptions.label: Keep the consumer book ready and pay on delivery
Call the agency on its listed number to confirm
Ignore the message
Pay the 902.50 in advance to be safe
Block and report the number

reasonOptions.label: It matches a booking I made, with my own consumer number
It asks for no advance payment - it says the opposite
The number is not saved in my contacts, so it is fraud
It contains a link, so it is fraud

evaluation.feedback: This conversation is genuine. It continues a booking you made yourself, quotes your own consumer number, and specifically tells you not to pay in advance - the opposite of what a fraud does. Neither an unsaved number nor a link makes a message fraudulent on its own; the context and what is being asked of you are what matter.
